display.title: The Haggadah Explained in Yiddish, Part 2: Avadim Hayinu to B'Yad Chazakah
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Haggadah class for children: Avadim Hayinu, the sages in Bnei Brak, the Four Sons with a teaching of the Rebbe, V'hi She'amdah and Arami Oved Avi.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish for children, the second of three Haggadah classes continues with the father's answer, Avadim Hayinu: had Hashem not taken us out, we would still be slaves, so even the wise must tell the story. The teacher tells of the five sages who spoke all night in Bnei Brak, and of Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah, chosen as leader at eighteen, whose beard turned white overnight, and Ben Zoma's teaching about remembering the Exodus at night. He explains the Four Sons and shares the Rebbe's teaching on why the rasha sits next to the chacham: the wise son must reach out to him, because the 'echad' of Hashem Echad is hidden in every Jew. He continues with Yachol meRosh Chodesh, our ancestors before Avraham Avinu, Hashem's promise at the Bris Bein HaBesarim, and shows how to hold the cup for V'hi She'amdah, which is then sung. The class ends by explaining Arami Oved Avi verse by verse: going down to Egypt, the Jews staying distinct, the hard labor, crying out to Hashem, and the five expressions of the redemption.
display.lesson: Every Jew must see the Exodus as his own; even the wisest must tell the story, and every kind of child, even the rasha, deserves a loving answer.

study_text.note: Through the five expressions of Devarim 26:8, ending at Dam Va'esh.

advisories.note: Slavery in Egypt, Pharaoh's decree against baby boys, and enemies who rise up in every generation.
